name: Forestiera

study_strategy.warning: Both can share the elbow-like branch architecture. Leaf width and seasonal habit are the fastest split.

quick_split: F. pubescens — broader elliptic/ovate leaves, some pubescence, winter-deciduous.
F. angustifolia — tiny narrow linear leathery leaves, densely twiggy, evergreen/semi-evergreen or drought-deciduous.

curation_status.visual_status: diagnostic_comparison_written; matched annotated photo pair pending

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Inspect a leafy mid-stem twig: paired/subopposite leaves on rigid, often elbow-like side branches. Then check the small apetalous flowers or dark one-seeded drupes. Do not identify by right-angle branching alone.
shared_traits: Woody shrubs with stiff, often paired angled branchlets
Small, simple, usually opposite to subopposite leaves
Small, inconspicuous flowers without showy petals, often appearing before new leaves
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Leaflessness, drought and pruning obscure habit; use comparable mature leaves from the same stem position.

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Very narrow, linear, leathery; blade margins often rolled under (revolute)
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Much broader elliptic, ovate, obovate to broadly lanceolate

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Firm, narrow blades, often revolute; pubescence not the principal clue
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Often scattered short hairs; broad blades with flatter margins

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Evergreen to semievergreen in favorable conditions, drought-deciduous when stressed
Very dense intricate twiggy habit with stiff near-right-angle branches
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Paired rigid lateral branches also make elbow-like angles

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Small apetalous flowers before leaf flush; dark one-seeded drupes
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Small apetalous flowers before leaf flush; dark purple drupes
species_comparison_matrix.weight: confirms genus, not a strong split

species_key.look: mid-stem mature leaves in focus, with ruler
species_key.if: linear, leathery, very narrow leaves, often rolled at margin

species_key.look: mid-stem mature leaves in focus, with ruler
species_key.if: broad elliptic/ovate/obovate leaves, sometimes visibly hairy

species_key.look: repeat on several shoots and check phenology
species_key.if: leaf shape conflicts or shrub is defoliated
species_key.then: Do not force species ID; photograph fruit/flowers, winter shoots, and revisit at leaf-out.

overlap_and_cautions: Both species make elbow-like paired branchlets; branch angles are not a species separator.
Drought can defoliate F. angustifolia; deciduous versus evergreen is seasonal support, not an absolute rule.
Young shoots and shade leaves can differ in width; compare mature leaves from matching mid-stem positions.
The dark drupe and apetalous flowers support genus recognition but alone do not separate these two species.
Avoid claiming an exact blade-width cutoff without independently verified measurements.

local_lookalike_routing.separate: Compare larger paired leaves and flower/fruit clusters; Forestiera typically has tiny apetalous flowers and a small drupe.
Check leaf arrangement and twig armature; do not rely on a skeletal shrub silhouette alone.
Ash has compound leaves and samaras; Forestiera has simple leaves and drupes.

targeted_handoff.question: Find an authoritative regional key with comparable measured mature leaf blade widths and confirm whether pubescence/revolute margins hold across local populations before adding numerical cutoffs.
